summary.en: If you live in Japan, are aged 20 to 59 and are neither in an employer's pension (Kosei Nenkin) nor a dependent spouse, you join the National Pension (Category 1), whether or not you are a student or a foreign national. Register at the ward office. People on Designated Activities for medical stay or long-stay tourism cannot join. Students (gakusei nofu tokurei) and people with low income can apply to defer or be exempted (to be checked).

lead.en: If you are 20 to 59 and are neither in an employee pension nor a dependent spouse, you join the National Pension.

text.en: If you leave a job: within 14 days from the day after. For other cases (arriving from abroad, turning 20), ask at the counter (to be checked).

text.en: Bring: the application form (National Pension insured-person notification). A document showing your basic pension number, or your My Number Card. Without the card: a document showing your My Number plus ID (driver's licence, passport, residence card, etc.). The insured person or the head of household files.

text.en: Students cannot use the regular exemption; they use the Student Payment Special Measure (gakusei nofu tokurei). Approved months count toward the pension eligibility period, but do not raise your pension unless you pay them back within 10 years. A Japanese-language school qualifies only if it is on the Japan Pension Service school list. Others (non-students, or students of a school not on the list) ask at the counter which exemption applies. Bring: the application form, a certificate of enrolment or a copy of your student ID, and your pension number or My Number Card (to be checked).
